results.term_definition: A light curve is a graph of the brightness, magnitude, or color of an object over time. Light curves are used to study a range of astronomical objects, e.g. variable stars, binary systems, exoplanets, X-ray binaries, or supernovae. Variations seen in the light curve help to classify the object and provide information such as the timescale or period of variability, which can be used to infer important information about it, such as the nature of the object, the source of energy input, or the types of physical processes that operate on it.
